The entire team at Brunnerne have been cooking and baking new exciting challenges for you to try, as we've expanded from a small home-bakery startup into an international unicorn as Brunnerne Inc.™, with this year's theme: "Brunnerne goes corporate". Whether you are a completely new CTF intern or a senior executive vice president of CTF competitions, there will be delicious challenges waiting for you. title: Haruulzangi CTF 2026 Qualifier
description:
Haruul Zangi CTF 2026 is organized by MNCERT/CC and the Haruulzangi CTF Team, representing the Mongolian CERT and cybersecurity community.
We are proud to announce the 14th edition of Haruul Zangi CTF and welcome participants from around the world. The competition aims to promote practical cybersecurity skills, encourage knowledge sharing, and strengthen collaboration within the global cybersecurity community.

Competition Format
The competition consists of three rounds:
Round 1 – Qualification (Online, Jeopardy)
•	Date: August 22, 2026 
•	Start Time: 09:00 (UTC+8) 
•	Duration: 24 hours 
Round 2 – Semi-Final (Onsite, Jeopardy)
•	Date: September 5, 2026 
•	Location: Mongolia 
Round 3 – Final (Onsite, Attack & Defense)
•	Date: September 24, 2026 
•	Location: Mongolia 

Challenge Categories
•	Pwn 
•	Web 
•	Forensics 
•	Cryptography 
•	Reverse Engineering 
•	Miscellaneous 
The challenges range from beginner to advanced difficulty, providing an engaging experience for both new and experienced CTF players.

Team Information
•	Teams may consist of up to 3 players. 
•	International participants are welcome. 

Qualification

The following teams will advance to the onsite Semi-Final:

The top 30 teams from the online Qualification Round, regardless of nationality.
The highest-ranked Mongolian high school team, if not already qualified through the top 30 overall ranking.
The highest-ranked Mongolian women’s team, if not already qualified through the top 30 overall ranking.

Among the international teams that qualify for the Semi-Final, the two highest-ranked teams, based on the online Qualification Round results, will be invited directly to the onsite Final.

If two international teams are invited to the Final, the top eight Mongolian teams from the Semi-Final will advance to the Final. The Final will consist of 10 teams in total and will be played in the Attack & Defense format.

Support for International Finalists
The organizers will provide the following support for the two invited international finalist teams:
•	Hotel accommodation during the onsite event. 
•	A daily allowance to cover meals and local expenses. 
Invited international teams are responsible for:
•	International and domestic transportation. 
•	Airfare and all other travel-related expenses. 
Visa invitation letters and supporting documents will be provided upon request.

Previous Challenges
Challenges from previous Haruul Zangi CTF competitions are publicly available in our GitHub organization:
https://github.com/haruulzangi
We look forward to welcoming teams from Mongolia and around the world to Haruul Zangi CTF 2026.
Good luck, have fun, and see you in Mongolia!

title: DefCamp Capture the Flag (D-CTF) 2026 Quals
description:
Mark Your Calendars! The DefCamp Capture the Flag (D-CTF) Qualification Phase is Locked and Loaded for 2026!

Get ready to dive into the most electrifying and audacious security CTF competition in Central and Eastern Europe—DefCamp Capture The Flag (D-CTF)!

This is where the sharpest hackers and IT masterminds come together to push their skills to the limit, battling it out with top CTF teams from around the globe. The mission? Secure a spot in the elite top 10 and ultimately conquer the D-CTF competition—or go down fighting!

Since 2011, DefCamp Capture the Flag has been the ultimate battleground for over 10,000 players. This annual, multi-stage event is open to all, but remember one crucial rule—hack or be hacked!

Event Highlights
Brace yourselves for an adrenaline-packed adventure with around 10 beginner-friendly challenges and 15 more difficult tasks that will test even the most seasoned players.

Format: Jeopardy
Play Format: Team-only
Genres: Crypto, Pwning, Reversing, Web, Forensics, Miscellaneous…
Language: English
Access: Open / Free for everyone
Difficulty: Entry Level - Easy - Medium - Hard - Insane

The Challenge Awaits

Tackle a variety of challenges across multiple categories.
Exploit system weaknesses, follow cryptic hints, and uncover hidden secrets.
Each challenge holds a unique flag in the format CTF{sha256 random message}. Capture it, submit it on our platform, and rack up your points.
CTF competitions are a thrilling mix of puzzles and challenges, including reverse-engineering, memory corruption, cryptography, web tech, and more. Solve them, capture the flag, and climb the leaderboard to victory!

Organizers & Partners
This epic event is brought to you by the Cyber Security Research Center from Romania (Asociatia Centrul de Cercetare in Securitate Informatica din Romania) under the banner of DefCamp, Romania's largest and most vibrant INFOSEC community.
prizes:
Best international teams in the global ranking and top teams from Romania are invited to the grand finale of DefCamp 2026, one of the largest and most anticipated cybersecurity conferences in the region.

The event will take place from November 18th-19th in Bucharest, Romania.

- Up to 3 teams from Romania will also secure a spot in the final
- Finalists will receive free tickets to DefCamp 2026.
- Full or partial accommodation reimbursement will be provided.

Main Prizes - International (for the final, onsite):
- 1st place: €1,536

title: WATCHLIST
description:
WATCHLIST is a 24-hour online Jeopardy CTF about digital investigation: forensics, OSINT, recon, and the hands-on work investigators actually do. It's a love letter to Person of Interest, narrated by The Machine.

There are 24 challenges across 6 categories: Forensics, Lab, OSINT, Recon, Trivia, and a Person of Interest story track that unlocks as you play.

It's made for beginners through intermediate players, so there's an easy way in and the difficulty climbs from there. Every challenge teaches a real, usable skill with tools people actually use, and the hints are written to teach you something, not just hand over the answer.

A few quick things:

Any tools are fine, including AI. They're helpers, not shortcuts, and they won't finish a challenge for you.
Teams of 1 to 6, and solo players are very welcome.
Free to play.

Prizes: $750 / $500 / $250 for the top three.

title: Hacker's Gambit 2026 (Round 1 – Online Qualifier)
description:
Round 1 – Online Qualifier (48 Hours)

The Online Qualifier is the first stage of Hackers Gambit 2026, designed to identify the most skilled cybersecurity teams from around the world. This 48-hour Jeopardy-style Capture The Flag (CTF) competition will challenge participants with a diverse set of real-world cybersecurity problems across multiple domains.

Participants will solve challenges in areas including Web Security, Cryptography, Reverse Engineering, Digital Forensics, Binary Exploitation (Pwn), Open Source Intelligence (OSINT), Steganography, and Miscellaneous. Each challenge carries a predefined score based on its difficulty level, and teams earn points by successfully capturing and submitting valid flags.

The competition will run continuously for 48 hours, allowing teams to strategize, collaborate, and solve challenges at their own pace within the competition window. A live leaderboard will be available throughout the event (subject to organizer discretion).

At the conclusion of the qualifier, participating teams may be required to submit technical write-ups explaining their solutions to selected challenges. These submissions will be reviewed by the organizing committee to verify the authenticity of solutions and ensure fair play.

Based on the final scores, write-up evaluation (if applicable), and adherence to the competition rules, the Top 15 teams will qualify for the 24-hour Offline Grand Finale at Jaihind College of Engineering, Kuran, where they will compete for the championship title, prizes, and recognition.

Key Highlights
Mode: Online
Duration: 48 Hours
Format: Jeopardy-style Capture The Flag (CTF)
Challenge Categories: Web Security, Cryptography, Reverse Engineering, Digital Forensics, Binary Exploitation, OSINT, Steganography, and Miscellaneous
Qualification: Top 15 teams advance to the Offline Grand Finale
Time: 2 October 2026 (12:00 PM IST) – 4 October 2026 (12:00 PM IST)

title: CDCTF 2026
description:
Crimson Defense CTF 2026 will be held on Saturday, October 3rd from 10am to 10pm CDT!

CDCTF is a virtual 12-hour Jeopardy-style Capture-the-Flag competition designed for collegiate-level players. All ability levels are welcome. 

This competition will not only provide satisfying challenges for seasoned players, but be a good introduction to CTFs for new ones!

CDCTF is a team competition, you may have up to four participants per team. Universities may have multiple teams representing their school.

There will be challenges of all difficulties representing the following categories: Reverse Engineering, Log & Network Traffic Analysis, Forensics, Password Cracking, Cryptography, Open Source Intelligence, Social Engineering, and AI!

Registration will open in August.

CDCTF is hosted and created by Crimson Defense Cyber Security Club at the University of Alabama.
prizes: Trophies are given to the top 3 teams (if US-based)

title: GaianSpace CTF 2026
description:
GaianSpace CTF, hosted by GaianSpace!
Challenges to secure ground and space systems through Web, Pwn, Forensics, Reverse, Network, Crypto and more.
Varied difficulties ensure fun for all skill levels. Hack the cosmos with us!

Location: Online
Event format: Jeopardy

First ever CTF scheduled:
Event start datetime: 2026.10.10 9:00pm (UTC)

Prizes: 1st Place, 2nd Place, 3rd Place, Write-up Prizes
prizes:
The top three teams and the best write-up will receive the following prizes:
1st Place: 100,000 SATS
2nd Place: 50,000 SATS
